How a transcript keeps its shape

A transcript is the full text of an item as one ordered stream of characters, written in reading order. Every feature in this system anchors to a position in that stream, which is why the stream must never be rebuilt differently from one run to the next.

The map records which sanitized node produced each span of transcript characters. Search hits, annotations, and rendered pages are all projections through that map. Nothing else stores a position, so nothing else can disagree with it.

Keeping one source of truth costs an extra parse at ingest time. That is a small price for a guarantee that a highlight saved today still points at the same words a year from now, even after the renderer changes.

The alternative is to store a position in each feature that needs one. Every such copy is a chance to drift, and drift in an annotation offset is silent. The reader sees a highlight over the wrong sentence and has no way to tell that the text moved rather than the highlight.
